CANDIDATE (for judging fit only, do not contact anyone):
Prabhavit Gupta, based in Venice, Italy. Holds an Italian EU long-term residence permit, so he needs NO sponsorship anywhere in the EU. ~3 years professional experience, all in European startups, most recently Lead Developer at FlowSpace (remote, London company) Mar 2024 to Jul 2026, now available. BA Philosophy/International Studies/Economics, Ca' Foscari Venice — no CS degree. Languages: English professional, Hindi native, Italian beginner (so any role needing professional Italian/German/French/Dutch/Spanish is OUT).
He can evidence: shipped AI agents in production (customer support agents, scraping/parsing tools, a CV-parsing tool in n8n + Eden AI); grew FlowSpace from 2,000 to 4,500+ users; led a live migration from Bubble.io to Next.js + Laravel; API integrations (Office RnD, Nexudus, Sendgrid, Google APIs, OpenAI/Anthropic, Eden AI, Clubee); GTM and lead-enrichment automation.

YOUR ARM: Track A — AI / automation engineering roles, discovered via ATS hosts.

DISCOVERY (run several WebSearch calls in parallel in one message where you can):
Use WebSearch with allowed_domains as a HARD host filter. Hosts to use:
["jobs.ashbyhq.com"], ["job-boards.greenhouse.io"], ["job-boards.eu.greenhouse.io"]
Queries to run (vary vocabulary, at least 8 distinct searches total across the hosts):
- AI automation engineer remote Europe
- AI solutions engineer remote EMEA
- applied AI engineer remote Europe
- automation engineer workflow remote Europe
- AI implementation engineer remote
- LLM engineer remote Europe
- AI engineer remote Italy
- agent engineer production remote EMEA

VERIFICATION — every row you return must come from a page you actually fetched:
- Normalise Ashby URLs to jobs.ashbyhq.com/<org>/<uuid> — strip ?embed=js, /application, ?utm_data=…, ?locationId=…
- Ashby HTML often returns a JS shell ("You need to enable JavaScript"). That means the FETCH failed, not that the role is closed. Fall back to the org's posting API: https://api.ashbyhq.com/posting-api/job-board/<org>?includeCompensation=true and ask it a TARGETED question (e.g. "does this board list a role called X, what is its location, is it remote, when was it published, and what compensation is stated?"). Do not ask it to "list all jobs" — the fetch truncates and will fabricate negatives.
- Greenhouse: if a single-posting fetch comes back describing MANY different jobs, the posting is CLOSED. Drop it. Use https://boards-api.greenhouse.io/v1/boards/<token>/jobs?content=true to corroborate when unsure.
- Read the ELIGIBILITY SENTENCE, not the word "Remote" in the title.

DROP (hard gates): requires a language beyond English; ML research/PhD/foundation-model training/CUDA/heavy data engineering (Spark, dbt, Airflow)/mobile native; staffing agencies, body shops and aggregators with no named end client (Jobgether especially); unpaid/equity-only/talent-pool listings; Staff/Principal/Head of/Director/people-managing Lead titles or 7+ years required; anything you could not confirm is live.

RETURN: a JSON array ONLY, no prose around it, of verified roles. Each object:
{"company":"", "role":"", "url":"", "location_wording":"exact eligibility sentence from the page", "comp":"as stated or empty", "posted":"as stated or empty", "basis":"employment|contract", "stack":"named tools from the JD", "seniority":"years or level asked for", "why_fit":"one honest sentence tying it to his real experience", "watchouts":"honest risks, e.g. timezone, seniority stretch, non-EU"}

Aim for 10-18 verified roles. Quality over count — a dead link costs him more than a missed role. If you end up with fewer than 8, run a second discovery pass with different vocabulary before returning.
